draft.title: How new species form
card: A species is a group of living things that can breed together and have fertile young. Populations of one species can be split apart by a barrier, such as the sea around an island. This is called isolation.
Isolated populations do not mix their genes. Each one faces its own conditions, such as different food, climate or predators, so different traits are favoured in each.
Random mutations (changes in DNA) also happen separately in each population. Natural selection can keep helpful ones in one population but not in the other.
Over many generations the populations become so different that they can no longer breed together to have fertile young. They are now separate species.
draft.remember: Isolation, different pressures and mutations, then no more breeding together: new species.

a.q: A few finches blown to a remote island form a new population. Which change is needed for them to become a new species?
opts: They become unable to breed with the mainland finches
They all grow larger than the mainland finches
They all learn to eat a new kind of food
They live apart from the mainland finches for a time
a.why: A new species exists only when the populations can no longer breed together. Living apart is the first step, but it is not enough alone, because isolated populations can still be able to breed if they meet.
a.clue: Think about the definition of a species.

b.q: Two populations of one frog species are split by a new desert. After thousands of years they meet again and cannot produce fertile young. What best explains this?
opts: Separate pressures and mutations changed each population
The desert caused the same mutations in both populations
The frogs chose not to mate with each other
Both populations kept mixing their genes across the desert
b.why: While apart, each population faced its own conditions and gained its own mutations, so they slowly became different. Mutations are random, so the desert did not cause the same ones in both. Mixing genes would have kept them one species.
b.clue: What happens to the genes of two populations kept apart?

a.best: They become unable to breed with the mainland finches
also_right: They live apart from the mainland finches for a time

b.best: Separate pressures and mutations changed each population

problems.detail: The question asks which change is 'needed' for speciation. The card teaches that isolation (living apart) is also needed, and the why admits it is 'the first step', so that option is defensible too. Reword to ask which change shows they have become a new species.

check.summary: Question a is ambiguous: asking what is 'needed' makes 'live apart for a time' defensible, since the card says isolation is required. Rewording to 'which change shows they are a new species' would fix it; the rest is accurate.
